overview:
Alabama's 4th District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of R+33. Robert Aderholt has held the seat since 1997 and is running again with a large financial advantage: about $750,000 on hand after raising over $1 million, against a Democratic challenger who has raised roughly $16,000 and has under $500 available. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give the Democrat about a 1% chance of winning.

With no polling to lean on, the forecast rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money, all of which point overwhelmingly to Aderholt. The expected margin is a heavy Republican win, with modest uncertainty given the absence of direct polling in the district.
